This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227
Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To Issue A Writ In
The Nature Of Mandamus Directing The Respondents To
Conclude The Acquisition Proceedings Initiated Pursuant
To Issuance Of The Notification In Laq:Sr:22/17-18 Dated
07.12.2017 By Issuing A Final Notification Immediately And
To Pass The Award Determining The Compensation And
Other Statutory Consequential Benefits Payable To The
Petitioners, If Necessary By Securing Reports From
Experts In Respect Of The Determination Of Value Of The
Land/Crops/Trees/Buildings/Structures Etc., And To Pay
Such Compensation To The Petitioners With Applicable
Rate Of Interest From The Date Of Taking Possession Of
Lands Forthwith, In The Interest Of Justice And Equity.

 Order
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned HCGP for the State.

2. These petitioners are before this Court aggrieved by the inaction of the respondents in not concluding the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7562 acquisition proceedings pursuant to the issuance of notification in LAQ:SR:22/17-18, dated 07.12.2017 and have not issued the final notification and neither they have passed any award for determination of compensation.

All the petitioners herein are the owners of different agricultural lands which were proposed to be acquired by the respondents under the very same preliminary notification and hence all the petitioners have a common grievance.
Hence they have filed this joint petition seeking the same relief.
3. The list of lands is mentioned in paragraph No.2 of the writ petition against each one of the petitioners along with the extent of land and the village.

It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioners that a preliminary notification came to be issued under Section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act, 2013') to acquire the lands for the purpose of construction of a canal under the 'Venkateshwara Lift Irrigation Scheme'.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
By virtue of the said acquisition, portions NC:
2024:KHC-D:7562 of the lands belonging to the petitioners were acquired and notices came to be issued to the petitioners being the landowners.
Pursuant to the notification and the notice, the possessions of the lands have been taken for the formation of the canal.

But however, till date it is the grievance of the petitioners that the final notification under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 has not been passed despite the same being extended from time to time, so also the acquisition proceedings have not been completed and not concluded and the compensation has not been paid to any of the petitioners herein.

Despite the petitioners making several representations produced at Annexures-C to C23, since no action has been taken by the respondents, hence they are were forced to approach this court seeking for the relief of conclusion of the acquisition proceedings.

4. It is the fundamental right and also the constitutional right of the petitioners to enjoy their property free from any kind of interference or obstructions as contemplated under Article 300A of the Constitution of India and if at all the State or any authority requires the land for NC:
2024:KHC-D:7562 larger public purposes, the same would have to be done in accordance with law by following due process of law.

In the present case, though the initial notification has been issued for acquisition of the property belonging to the petitioners, notices being issued, the final notification has not been issued concluded and no order of compensation or award is passed and nothing has been paid to the petitioners, who are farmers and landowners of the lands which have been acquired by the respondents.
5. Admittedly, their lands have been acquired, preliminary notification has been issued and lands have been utilized for the purpose of which it is sought to be acquired.

Nothing much remains for the State to do except for following the due process of law by initiating and concluding the final acquisition proceedings, conduct an inquiry and pass suitable award by awarding compensation and disburse the same to their respective land losers/petitioners.

Accordingly, this court proceed to pass the following :

5 ORDER (i) Petition is allowed.

(iii) The same shall be done in accordance with law after determination of the value of the land, so also the land, crops and trees, building, structures, if any, existing on the lands as on date of acquisition.

(iv) Since the land has been acquired and taken away from the land losers' way back in the year 2017, the final conclusion of the acquisition proceedings shall be completed within an outer limit of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
